headline: This law makes permanent some federal IT spending rules and extends a federal data center consolidation program through fiscal year 2020.
what_it_does: It removes the expiration date on several requirements from a 2014 defense authorization law. Those requirements have the White House budget office publish a list of major federal technology investments with cost, schedule, and performance details. They also require agency chief information officers to review high-risk IT investments that stay high-risk for four quarters in a row, and they require a process for agencies to review their IT portfolios. The law also extends the Federal Data Center Consolidation Initiative through fiscal year 2020.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that buy or run information technology
who_it_affects.how: They must keep following the requirements to report major IT investments, review persistently high-risk projects, and review their IT portfolios without the rules expiring.

who_it_affects.group: Chief information officers and program managers in federal agencies
who_it_affects.how: They must continue conducting risk management reviews of IT investments that carry a high risk rating for four consecutive quarters.

who_it_affects.group: The public and taxpayers who follow federal technology spending
who_it_affects.how: The Office of Management and Budget must keep publishing a list of major federal IT investments with data on cost, schedule, and performance.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that operate data centers
who_it_affects.how: They continue to take part in the data center consolidation effort, which now runs through fiscal year 2020.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed into law on November 21, 2017; the data center extension runs through fiscal year 2020.
